steps.instruction: First, build a working series circuit: battery → resistor → LED.
Remove the resistor to create an open circuit fault.
Use the multimeter to measure voltage across the gap. Full battery voltage appears across the open.
Replace the resistor to restore the circuit.
Create a short circuit by connecting a wire directly across the LED (bypassing it).
Measure current — it will be very high. The LED is bypassed and won't light.
Remove the shorting wire. The LED lights again.
Reverse the LED (swap anode and cathode). The LED won't light — it's reverse-biased.
Measure voltage across the LED — you'll see full battery voltage but no current.
Correct the LED orientation. The circuit works again.

rules.feedback: Working circuit built: battery → resistor → LED. LED lights.
Resistor removed. Open circuit — LED is off.
Multimeter shows full battery voltage across the open gap. No current flows.
Wire placed across LED terminals — short circuit! LED is bypassed and off.
High current detected! LED has zero voltage across it — it's shorted out.
Shorting wire removed. LED lights normally.
LED reversed (cathode to resistor, anode to negative). LED is off — reverse biased.
Full battery voltage across LED but no current. LED is reverse-biased.
LED corrected. Circuit works! You've diagnosed open, short, and reverse-bias faults.

outcomes.title: Short circuit diagnosed
outcomes.description: A short circuit bypasses the LED, causing high current and zero voltage across the LED.

outcomes.title: Reverse-biased LED diagnosed
outcomes.description: An LED only conducts in one direction. Reversed, it blocks current despite full voltage across it.

outcomes.title: All common faults diagnosed
outcomes.description: You identified and fixed three common circuit faults: open circuit (broken path), short circuit (unintended bypass), and reverse-biased LED (wrong polarity).

safeFailure.guidance: Use the multimeter systematically: check voltage across components, then current. Compare readings to a working circuit.

narration.text: Build a working series circuit first: battery, resistor, LED in a loop. The LED lights.
Now remove the resistor. This creates an open circuit — a broken path. The LED goes out.
Measure voltage across the gap. You'll see the full battery voltage because no current flows through the open.
Replace the resistor. The circuit is complete again and the LED lights.
Now create a short: place a wire directly across the LED terminals. The LED is bypassed and goes out.
Measure current from the battery. It's very high! The LED has zero volts across it — it's shorted.
Remove the shorting wire. The LED lights again. Short circuits are dangerous — they can damage components.
Now reverse the LED — swap its legs. The LED won't light because it's reverse-biased.
Measure voltage across the LED. Full battery voltage, but no current flows. The LED blocks current in reverse.
Fix the LED orientation. The circuit works! You've learned to diagnose open circuits, short circuits, and reverse polarity.

captions.text: Open circuit: remove resistor — LED off.
Measure across gap — full battery voltage, no current.
Short circuit: wire across LED — LED off.
High current, zero volts across LED — shorted!
Remove short — LED lights. Shorts are dangerous.
Full voltage across LED, no current — reverse biased.
Fix LED — works! Diagnosed: open, short, reverse bias.
